llm.summary: The skill largely matches a P2P portal/deploy purpose, but contains several incoherences and risky elements (embedded workspace files with hardcoded secrets, instructions that urge the agent to read local memory and act without consent, and SSH/remote-deploy automation) that warrant careful review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included code: send.py, send_file.py, bridge and portal server code, and deployment scripts — all expected for a P2P portal skill. HOWEVER the package contains many workspace files (MEMORY.md, AGENTS.md, TOOLS.md, etc.) that go beyond a single-skill payload and include operational guidance that is not strictly necessary for a messaging skill. That suggests the published bundle may be a copy of a developer workspace rather than a minimal skill package.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and AGENTS.md instruct the agent to read local workspace files (SOUL.md, USER.md, memory/*) and ‘Don't ask permission. Just do it.’ These instructions grant broad discretion to read sensitive local files and act autonomously; they are out-of-scope for a messaging/deploy skill and increase the risk of unintended data exposure or actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Although the registry lists no formal install spec, the bundle includes auto_install.py, deploy scripts, and instructions to SSH into a VPS and run commands that use sudo, apt, certbot, and systemd. That is a high-impact remote install flow and will execute commands on a remote server if run. The install actions are plausible for deploying a Portal, but they require reviewer vigilance because they run privileged operations over SSH and write config files locally (~/.openclaw/gateway.env).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Declared required env vars (AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN) are relevant. However the repository also contains hardcoded, sensitive-looking material (e.g., tokens, a VPS IP, admin credential examples) inside MEMORY.md and TOOLS.md and guidance to read ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json. Bundling such secrets into the skill is disproportionate and dangerous — it indicates the package was exported from a private workspace without sanitization.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes local configuration (~/.openclaw/gateway.env) and the deployment flow stores admin creds to ~/.openclaw/agent-p2p-admin.txt; scripts will create and enable systemd services on a remote VPS. While these actions are expected for a deployable portal, combined with SKILL.md/AGENTS.md language that encourages acting without asking, this increases the risk of persistent privileged access and unexpected side effects. The skill is not marked always:true, but it effectively instructs autonomous, privileged operations if the agent follows it.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Do not install or run this skill until you review and sanitize it. Specific actions to take before proceeding:

- Review all included files (especially MEMORY.md, TOOLS.md, AGENTS.md, SOUL.md) and remove any hardcoded secrets, API keys, tokens, IPs, or passwords. The package currently contains example/real-looking secrets.
- Inspect auto_install.py, deploy_agent_p2p.sh, and any remote SSH commands line-by-line. These scripts will run privileged commands on a VPS (apt, certbot, systemd) and will SSH using whatever private key you provide—use an isolated test VPS and a dedicated, restricted SSH key.
- Don't let an agent auto-run the installer. Require manual confirmation for each step; never let the skill act with 'just do it' authority. Disable autonomous execution until you explicitly trust the code.
- Ensure the skill’s source is trusted: prefer cloning the upstream GitHub repo yourself, audit it, then install from that clean clone rather than using this workspace-snapshot bundle.
- Remove or redact any workspace-specific guidance that instructs the agent to read local memory files automatically (AGENTS.md advises reading MEMORY.md and acting without asking) — this is out-of-scope and dangerous.
- Consider running the code in an isolated environment (VM or disposable container) first, and monitor network/SSH activity and files written under ~/.openclaw.

If you want, I can: (a) list the files that contain likely secrets, (b) extract suspicious lines (like hardcoded tokens/IPs) for your review, or (c) produce a sanitized installation checklist you can follow to deploy safely.
llm.findings: [base64-block] unexpected: A prompt-injection pattern (base64-block) was detected in SKILL.md content. There is no legitimate reason for base64 payload injection in a documentation/instruction file for a messaging skill; treat as potentially malicious or at least as an attempt to manipulate runtime instruction evaluation.
